within.statement: When a URL is submitted for shortening, the product creates a short URL for it using either a generated slug or a custom alias.

claims.tier_basis: This is a documented default: whether an omitted shortlink yields an automatically generated one changes what a script must send to /api/new. A person writing against the API would act differently if it were other than stated. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

claims.quote:
A missing `<expiry_delay>` or a value of 0 will disable
expiry.
claims.statement: Links created with expiry_delay omitted or set to 0 do not expire.
claims.tier_basis: If false, links would expire or persist against the operator's intent, but a person creating links through the API acts directly on this parameter's behaviour, and staff could set an explicit expiry value or manage links by hand, which the reliance statement treats as cheap for the expiry item. No stated threshold reaches expiry behaviour. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

claims.quote: Multiple links can be created in a single request by sending an array of objects like the example below.
claims.statement: A single request to /api/new carrying an array of objects results in multiple links being created.
claims.tier_basis: If false, a caller sending an array to /api/new would create fewer links than expected, and anyone writing against the API would do so differently on the strength of this documented request format. Failure on its own changes nothing about price or terms, and the API is an item the buyer only uses on the practice's inference. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

claims.quote: Except for malformed requests or internal server errors, the HTTP status code is always `200`.
claims.statement: In operation, every request the target receives receives HTTP status 200, except malformed requests and those causing internal server errors.
claims.tier_basis: If false, a developer integrating against the service would handle status codes differently, since the documented status-code behaviour is exactly the kind of API surface a documentation-reliant buyer codes against. No stated threshold reaches HTTP status behaviour, and the API itself is an item the buyer uses on the practice's inference. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

claims.quote: This is faster, and the preferred way of doing pagination.
claims.statement: Pagination requests to /api/all that use the page_after parameter complete faster than pagination requests that use the alternative method.
claims.tier_basis: If false, the buyer loses nothing: both pagination methods work, and the claim only says one is faster and preferred, so a developer choosing between them is inconvenienced at most. Neither the buyer's stated thresholds nor any reliance item turns on relative pagination speed. Rated on the scale alone.
